questions.question: A boat takes 21 minutes to go 12.6 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 7 : 2. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 43.2 km upstream and 38.88 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Upstream Distance = 12.6 km

Time taken = 21 min 

The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 7 : 2.

**Formula Used:**

{Speed} = {{Distance} over {Time}}

**Calculations:**

Take the speed of the boat in still water and stream as 7x and 2x respectively.

So, we have, the Upstream speed = 7x - 2x = 5x

{Speed} = {{Distance} over {Time}}\ implies 5x = {12.6 over {21 over 60}}\ implies 5x = {12.6 times 60 over 21}\ implies 5x = {756 over 21}\ implies x = {36 over 5}\ implies x = 7.2 

So, speed of boat in still water is 50.4 km/h and speed of boat in stream is 14.4 km/h.

Downstream speed = 50.4 + 14.4 = 64.8 km/h

Downstream distance = 38.88 km

{Downstream time}= {38.88 over 64.8}\ implies {Downstream time} = 0.6 h 

Upstream speed = 50.4 - 14.4 = 36 km

Upstream distance = 43.2 km

{Upstream time}= {43.2 over 36}\ implies {Upstream time} = 1.2 h 

So, Total Time = 0.6 + 1.2 = 1.8 hours

**Therefore, the boat will take a total of 1.8 hours to go 43.2 km upstream and 38.88 km downstream.**

questions.question: The centre of curvature of a convex mirror is located at +18 cm, as per New Cartesian Sign convention. Its focus is at
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The New Cartesian Sign Convention has several rules:**
 
• The object is always placed to the left of the mirror.
 
• This means all distances measured to the **right of the mirror (along + x-axis) are taken as positive, while those measured to the left are taken as negative.**
 
• The heights measured upwards and perpendicular to the principal axis are taken as positive.
 
• Those measured downwards are taken as negative.
 
• For a spherical mirror (convex or concave),** the radius of curvature (R) is twice the focal length (f).**
 
• This is expressed in the mirror formula as** R = 2f.**
 
• Given that the centre of curvature **(which equals the radius of curvature) of a convex mirror is located at +18 cm, the focal length would be half of this.**
 
• However, because the **mirror is convex, the focus is virtual and is found on the same side as the light being reflected.**
 
• According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, this side of the mirror is the negative side.
 
• So, the focus of the mirror would be at** 9 cm.**

Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 5(1)/(2) hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P can fill (3)/(4) part of a tank in 18 hours

 pipe Q can fill (3)/(5) part of the same tank in 12 hours. 

**Formula used:**

Capacity = time × efficiency

**Calculation:**

Pipe P can fill whole a tank = 18times ({4over3})= 24 hours 

Pipe Q can fill whole a tank = 12times ({5over3})​= 20 hours

Total capacity of a tank = LCM(24,20) = 120 units

P's efficiency = 120over 24 = 5 units

P's efficiency = 120over 20 = 6 units

Pipe (P + Q)’s 1 hour's work = 5 + 6 = 11 units

Both P and Q were kept open for 4 hours, then both were closed,⇒

⇒ Pipe (P + Q)’s 4 hours work = 4 x 11 = 44 units

Now, Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 5(1)/(2) hours

Then,

⇒ R's efficiency(-) = 44over{11over 2} = 8 units 

Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:

⇒ Total efficiency of P, Q and R = 5 + 6 - 8 = 3 

⇒ Total time taken = 120over 3 =40 hours

so, It will take 40 hours to fill the tank when all three pipes are opened simultaneously.

Hence, **'Option 4'** is the correct answer.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 6 years more than 3 times the present age of the son. After 2 years, 2 times the father's age will be 7 years less than 5 times the son's age. The difference (in years) between the ages of the father and the son is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the present age of the father be F years.

Let the present age of the son be S years.

F + S = 3S + 6

F = 3S - S + 6

F = 2S + 6 (Equation 1)

After 2 years:

Father's age will be F + 2 and Son's age will be S + 2

2 × (F + 2) = 5 × (S + 2) - 7

2F + 4 = 5S + 10 - 7

2F + 4 = 5S + 3

2F = 5S + 3 - 4

2F = 5S - 1 (Equation 2)

Substitute Equation 1 (F = 2S + 6) into Equation 2:

2 × (2S + 6) = 5S - 1

4S + 12 = 5S - 1

12 + 1 = 5S - 4S

13 = S

Now, substitute the value of S back into Equation 1:

F = 2S + 6

F = 2 × (13) + 6

F = 26 + 6 = 32

So, the father's present age (F) = 32 years.

Difference = Father's age - Son's age = 32 - 13 = 19 years

**∴ The difference between the ages of the father and the son is 19 years.**

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of British India when the Rowlatt Act was passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Lord Chelmsford'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the government under the **period of Lord Chelmsford.**
 
• It was** passed in February 1919.** Every single Indian member of the Central Legislative Council opposed it.
 
• **The act authorised the government to imprison any suspect without trial and conviction in the court of law**.
 
• It enables the government **to suppress the habeas corpus**.
 
• They wanted to **replace the provision of repression during wartime Defence of India Act 1915** by a permanent law.
 
• It was based on the report of Justice S.A.T. Rowlatt’s Committee of 1918.
 
• The act was resented by the Indian public and opposed by all Indian members of the Council.
 
• **Gandhi organised a protest movement which led to the Massacre of Amritsar (April 1919)**.
 
• The act was never actually implemented.
